title: Fly production target has no persistent volume — every deploy wipes the entire leaderboard
description:
**Severity:** critical · **Effort:** S · **Dimension:** backend-build
**Location:** `fly.toml:1-20 (no [[mounts]])`

**Issue:** The server writes SQLite to DATA_DIR=/data (Dockerfile:41 sets ENV DATA_DIR=/data; index.js:11-18 reads it and opens /data/leaderboard.db). fly.toml has no [[mounts]] section, so /data lives on the machine's ephemeral rootfs, which Fly re-creates from the image on every `fly deploy`, image update, or host migration. auto_stop_machines=false / min_machines_running=1 keeps one machine warm but does nothing to survive a redeploy. Commit b759d4d ('Switch to SQLite with better-sqlite3 for self-hosted deployments') confirms the whole point of the SQLite migration was persistence, yet the primary hosted target silently loses all leaderboard rows (and any collected player emails) on every code deploy, with no backup path.

**Fix:** Create a Fly volume (`fly volumes create data --size 1 --region syd`) and add `[[mounts]] source = "data", destination = "/data"` so DATA_DIR persists. docker-compose already mounts ./data:/data, so only the Fly config is missing it. Optionally add litestream for backup since one volume is still a single point of failure.

**Impact:** Guaranteed silent, total loss of all scores (and stored emails) on every deploy of the primary hosted target — the exact opposite of the persistence the SQLite migration was made for. Data value is low but the loss is total and invisible until users notice an empty board.
_Source: docs/review/aaa-audit.md_
notes: Config fixed: [[mounts]] gd_data->/data added to fly.toml. REQUIRES one-time ops step before next deploy: 'fly volumes create gd_data --region syd --size 1'. Kept open until volume exists + persistence verified on a real deploy (can't test locally).
close_reason: Resolved for the actual (non-Fly) setup. App self-hosts via docker-compose with ./data:/data bind mount; SQLite at /data/leaderboard.db persists on the host. Verified LIVE locally: built hardened image (non-root node, npm ci), ran container, POSTed a score, 'docker restart', score survived; frontend+API serve at :3000. fly.toml [[mounts]] kept only for any future Fly deploy. No volume/sudo needed.

title: No rate limiting on the unauthenticated write endpoint + unbounded no-email inserts
description:
**Severity:** high · **Effort:** S · **Dimension:** backend-build
**Location:** `server/index.js:35-36, 99`

**Issue:** There is no rate limiting anywhere (no express-rate-limit, no proxy throttle). The no-email submit path (insertWithoutEmail, index.js:99) INSERTs a brand-new row on every request with no dedup or cap, so a loop of anonymous POSTs grows the table without bound. Combined with the wide-open validation (see the client-authoritative finding), a single script can both spam garbage into the public top-10 and slowly grow the table until the container's rootfs (ephemeral today — no volume) or, once a volume/host mount exists, that disk fills and SQLite writes start failing. GET always returns only top-10, so the bloat is invisible until it breaks writes.

**Fix:** Add express-rate-limit (e.g. 5 submits/min/IP) on POST /api/leaderboard. Independently bound storage: keep only top-N rows (delete below rank N after insert) or require email so the UPDATE-if-higher dedup (index.js:88-97) caps rows per player. Cap body with `express.json({ limit: '4kb' })`.

**Impact:** An unauthenticated public write endpoint with no throttle lets one attacker (or a buggy client retry loop) both bury legitimate entries and, given time, exhaust disk to wedge the DB. The abuse surface is the sharp part; the disk-fill is a slow secondary consequence given small rows.
_Source: docs/review/aaa-audit.md_
close_reason: express-rate-limit on POST /api/leaderboard (10/min/IP) + express.json 8kb body cap + CORS scoped to dev origins. Verified live (429 after budget).

title: Leaderboard is fully client-authoritative with almost no input validation — trivial to cheat, and…
description:
**Severity:** high · **Effort:** M · **Dimension:** backend-build
**Location:** `server/index.js:77-100`

**Issue:** POST /api/leaderboard trusts a client-computed score (App.tsx:63 sets score: finalScoreBreakdown.finalScore; App.tsx:69-72 POSTs it) with no auth, no signature, and no server-side re-derivation. The only guard is `!name || typeof score !== 'number'` (index.js:80), which passes NaN, Infinity, negatives, and floats (all typeof 'number' → stored into an INTEGER NOT NULL column, producing garbage or a constraint-violation 500), and never checks name is a string (a truthy object/array passes `!name`, then throws inside the try at .run() → 500). Neither name nor email has a length cap — express.json's default limit is ~100KB, so a ~99KB name stores fine. `curl -X POST /api/leaderboard -d '{"name":"AAA…(99KB)","score":999999999}'` pins the top of every player's board.

**Fix:** Validate at the boundary: reject unless `Number.isInteger(score) && score >= 0 && score <= MAX_PLAUSIBLE_SCORE`; require `typeof name === 'string'`, trim, and cap length (e.g. 24 chars); require email to match a simple regex + length cap. Add `express.json({ limit: '4kb' })`. For real integrity, issue a signed per-run token at game start and validate an HMAC of the run, or derive score from server-observed events — a 90s single-player game can't be fully cheat-proof, but clamping + a signed token raises the bar from 'one curl' to meaningful effort.

**Impact:** The leaderboard has zero integrity: anyone can set any name to any score in one request, and NaN/Infinity/negative/object inputs yield garbage rows or 500s. For a tool shown to NZ Police stakeholders, an absurd/garbage top-10 is an embarrassing, trivially triggered failure.
_Source: docs/review/aaa-audit.md_
close_reason: Server-side validateSubmission() (server/validate.js): rejects non-int/NaN/Infinity/negative/over-cap scores, caps name 1-24, validates+lowercases email, ignores client timestamp. Verified live (all 6 malformed payloads -> 400). Unit-tested (server/validate.test.js).

title: No music or ambient bed — a 90s tension shift is atmospherically flat

Optional thematic win: occasional synthesized police-radio-chatter blips. A single looping node set costs almost nothing and respects mute automatically via masterGain routing.

**Impact:** Transforms feel from 'tech demo with beeps' to an arcade shift with atmosphere and tension; large perceived-quality lift.

title: Siren wail decays into a faint dead ~900 Hz tone after 5.6s of continuous use
description:
**Severity:** high · **Effort:** M · **Dimension:** audio
**Location:** `utils/audio.ts:206-212`

**Issue:** sirenStart schedules the wail as discrete gain curves: one setValueCurveAtTime over 1.4s (lines 179/189), then scheduleSirenLoop (209) adds only 3 more (i=1..3) at now+1.4/2.8/4.2 — coverage ends at ~5.6s. After the last curve, each AudioParam holds its final sample: buildSirenCurve(true)[63]=sin(0.984pi)*0.9 ~= 0.045 and buildSirenCurve(false)[63]=max(0,sin(1.484pi))*0.9 = 0, so osc2 (650 Hz) goes fully silent and osc1 (900 Hz) holds a faint steady tone — the two-tone wail dies. This would be masked by the intended 5s cap, but PLAYER_SIREN_MAX_DURATION (constants.ts:30), DT_SIREN_DRAIN_PER_SEC (constants.ts:185) and sirenStartTimeRef (Game.tsx:125,288) are never consumed, and the siren has no boost-charge drain while active (Game.tsx:397-403 gate charge changes on !isSirenActive). So the player can hold E indefinitely and the thematically central police siren audibly dies after 5.6s while staying mechanically on.

**Fix:** Make the wail self-sustaining: drive the two siren gains from a low-frequency (~0.7 Hz) OscillatorNode routed through a GainNode into each osc's gain, or oscillate osc frequency directly. This never expires, is fewer lines than buildSirenCurve + scheduleSirenLoop (delete both), and removes any dependence on a duration cap. Verify by holding the siren >10s.

**Impact:** Fixes an audible failure of a thematically central, frequently-used mechanic (the police siren) in an NZ Police training tool; since the siren has no drain, players will realistically leave it on and hear the dead tone for most of a 90s shift.
_Source: docs/review/aaa-audit.md_
close_reason: Siren rewritten to a continuous LFO sweeping oscillator frequency (utils/audio.ts sirenStart/sirenStop); removes the finite setValueCurve scheduling that decayed to a dead ~900Hz tone after ~5.6s. LFO torn down in sirenStop.

title: Blanket reduced-motion reset makes the Speed mini-game unwinnable
description:
**Severity:** high · **Effort:** M · **Dimension:** accessibility
**Location:** `components/mini-games/PrecisionSlider.tsx:index.html:459-466; PrecisionSlider.tsx:59-66,78-87,8-15`

**Issue:** PrecisionSlider is a timing game: the player presses SPACE/STOP while a CSS-animated slider (.animate-slider, 2.5s linear infinite, PrecisionSlider.tsx:84-86) is inside the 37.5-62.5% zone. The universal reduced-motion rule (index.html:460-462) sets animation-duration:0.01ms !important and animation-iteration-count:1 !important on *, so the slider never traverses the zone (no fill-mode leaves it at left:auto ~0). STOP then reads a miss, and the 4s failTimer (lines 9-13) forces onComplete(false). Reduced-motion users cannot pass Speed enforcement (only avoidable by choosing the lower-reward Warn).

**Fix:** Do not zero gameplay-critical animations with the universal selector — scope the reset with :not(), or drive the slider from a requestAnimationFrame loop (as QuickTimeEvent.tsx:10-26 already does) at a playable, non-vestibular speed, and/or provide a click-in-zone alternative under reduced-motion.

**Impact:** An accessibility setting silently makes a required interaction unwinnable — reduced-motion should never remove function (WCAG 2.3.3 intent). Reduced-motion players are pushed to the lower-reward Warn path or fail outright.
_Source: docs/review/aaa-audit.md_
close_reason: PrecisionSlider rebuilt: slider driven by requestAnimationFrame (direct DOM write, no per-frame re-render) instead of a CSS keyframe, so the global prefers-reduced-motion reset no longer freezes it and forces a loss. title: focus:outline-none with no focus-visible fallback makes keyboard focus invisible on modal buttons
description:
**Severity:** high · **Effort:** S · **Dimension:** accessibility
**Location:** `components/mini-games/SituationalJudgement.tsx:SituationalJudgement.tsx:189; Game.tsx:43,49`

title: Canvas screen-shake ignores prefers-reduced-motion
description:
**Severity:** high · **Effort:** S · **Dimension:** accessibility
**Location:** `utils/gameRenderer.ts:313-323 (Game.tsx:433-435,625,860,888,1086)`

**Issue:** shakeX/shakeY are computed from camera.shake (gameRenderer.ts:313-314) and applied to ctx.translate every frame (line 323) with no reduced-motion guard. camera.shake is set to 10 on successful Enforce (Game.tsx:888) and mini-game success (1086), incremented +4 capped at 10 on road-edge collisions (625), and forced to >=4 while boosting (860). The global prefers-reduced-motion CSS reset (index.html:459-466) only zeroes CSS animation/transition and cannot touch canvas rendering. The same driving code already checks reduced-motion for car rotation (Game.tsx:433-435), proving the check was understood but not applied to shake.

**Fix:** Compute reduceMotion = window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches once (cached/subscribed, not per-frame) and force shakeX=shakeY=0 in drawGame, or gate every camera.shake assignment in Game.tsx behind it.

**Impact:** Full-screen camera shake is a vestibular trigger; users who set reduced-motion still get it. WCAG 2.3.3 and the spirit of 2.3.1; a shipped-AAA bar treats blanket shake as a safety issue.
_Source: docs/review/aaa-audit.md_
close_reason: Canvas screen-shake now zeroed when prefers-reduced-motion (module-scoped cached matchMedia in gameRenderer.ts drawGame). DOM/CSS animations already covered by the blanket reduced-motion reset. File: utils/gameRenderer.ts.

title: Viewport disables pinch-zoom (user-scalable=no)
description:
**Severity:** high · **Effort:** S · **Dimension:** accessibility
**Location:** `index.html:5 (HUD.tsx:350,354)`

**Issue:** The viewport meta is content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, viewport-fit=cover, user-scalable=no". user-scalable=no prevents pinch-to-zoom on Android/Chromium, and the UI uses very small type (HUD.tsx:350,354 text-[10px]; text-xs across menus/forms) low-vision users cannot magnify.

**Fix:** Remove user-scalable=no (do not add maximum-scale); keep width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover. body already sets touch-action:none (index.html:470) to stop gesture interference during gameplay, so page zoom need not be suppressed.

**Impact:** Low-vision mobile users cannot enlarge any screen (menus, tutorial, score-submission form, leaderboard); direct WCAG 1.4.4 Resize Text and 1.4.10 Reflow failure. One-line fix.
_Source: docs/review/aaa-audit.md_

title: In-game modals (RIDS choice + mini-game) have no dialog semantics, focus management, or focus trap
description:
**Severity:** high · **Effort:** M · **Dimension:** accessibility
**Location:** `components/Game.tsx:MiniGameModal.tsx:31-37; Game.tsx:36-56, 936-955`

**Issue:** Both progression-gating modals are plain divs (MiniGameModal.tsx:31, Game.tsx:36) with no role="dialog", aria-modal, or aria-labelledby, and neither moves focus into the modal, traps Tab, or restores focus on close. RidsChoiceModal is keyboard-operable only via a window-keydown handler (Game.tsx:936-955) that mutates ridsChoiceSelection state; the mini-games (e.g. SituationalJudgement.tsx:144-162) also listen on window, so keyboard 'works' but through a non-DOM path. Mark the background game inert/aria-hidden while a modal is open so MuteToggle/HUD leave the tab order.

**Impact:** Screen-reader and keyboard-only players cannot perceive a blocking modal appeared and can tab out of it; violates 4.1.2, 2.4.3, 1.3.1. Every RIDS interaction routes through these modals, so this blocks the primary game loop for AT users.

title: No service worker — the installable fullscreen PWA has zero offline capability
description:
**Severity:** high · **Effort:** M · **Dimension:** mobile-pwa
**Location:** `public/manifest.json:1-19 (display:fullscreen L6; A2HS metas index.html:7-11; no SW registration anywhere in repo)`

**Issue:** A repo-wide search for serviceWorker/registerSW/workbox/sw.js and navigator.serviceWorker.register returns nothing; package.json has no vite-plugin-pwa, and the built dist/ contains only index.html, manifest.json, icon.svg and assets/ (no sw.js). Yet manifest.json declares display:fullscreen (line 6) with A2HS metas present (index.html:7-11), advertising an installable chrome-less app. With no service worker and no precache, launching the installed home-screen icon on no/flaky network yields a white screen (compounded by the runtime CDN dependencies above). A 90-second self-contained arcade game is an ideal offline PWA candidate.

**Fix:** Add a minimal service worker (vite-plugin-pwa / Workbox) that precaches the app shell — index.html, the bundled JS/CSS, self-hosted fonts, and icon — with a cache-first strategy, and register it on load. This depends on the CDN finding: assets must be first-party before they can be cached.

**Impact:** Turns the manifest's installability claim into a real offline-capable installed app, instead of a home-screen icon that breaks the first time the network hiccups.
_Source: docs/review/aaa-audit.md_
close_reason: Added vite-plugin-pwa (Workbox): precaches the fully self-hosted app shell (18 entries ~674KB: JS/CSS/woff2/icons/HTML) with SPA navigateFallback (/api/* denied). Installable PWA now works offline. Verified headlessly: SW controls the page, then a reload with network cut still mounts the menu (23 nodes, 'Start Shift'), zero page errors. Files: vite.config.ts, package.json.

title: Four core HUD meters (boost charge, vigilance, siren energy, district deterrence) are hidden on…

**Issue:** The bottom-center HUD cluster — Speedometer, ASSIST count, the BOOST/SIREN charge bar, and (separately) the VIGILANCE meter — is wrapped in `[@media(pointer:coarse)]:hidden` (lines 391 and 394), so it disappears on every touch device. At minimum keep a boost-charge indicator and a district-deterrence readout visible on phones.

title: Production render path depends on three third-party CDNs — Tailwind Play CDN (dev-only), Google…
description:
**Severity:** high · **Effort:** M · **Dimension:** mobile-pwa
**Location:** `index.html:18-19, 20-28 (dist/index.html:18-19, 461-469 corroborates; production ships dist via Dockerfile:14,34,52)`

**Issue:** The in-scope source index.html hard-codes three external dependencies on the critical render path: the Google Fonts stylesheet (line 18), Tailwind's Play CDN `<script src="https://cdn.tailwindcss.com">` (line 19), and a React importmap pointing at https://aistudiocdn.com (lines 20-28). vite build does NOT strip any of them — dist/index.html preserves fonts+Tailwind (18-19) and the importmap (461-469) beside the bundled /assets/index-*.js (470), and the Dockerfile builds that dist (`RUN npm run build`) and serves it in production (`COPY --from=builder /app/dist`; `node index.js`). cdn.tailwindcss.com is the Play CDN, which Tailwind's own docs state is not for production: it ships a large JS compiler that regenerates CSS in the browser on every load. Every React component in this codebase (HUD.tsx, TouchControls.tsx, RotateDevicePrompt.tsx) is styled entirely with Tailwind utility classes, and the <style> block relies on `theme('colors.*')` calls, so without that runtime compiler nothing renders correctly. Online this works but with first-paint jank and FOUC; on a flaky/absent connection an installed mobile PWA instance shows a white screen.

**Fix:** Move Tailwind to a build-time dependency (PostCSS/Vite plugin) so CSS compiles to a bundled first-party stylesheet and the runtime theme() calls resolve at build; self-host Orbitron + Rajdhani as woff2 with font-display:swap; delete the dead React importmap (React is already in the vite bundle). This makes every asset first-party — the prerequisite for real precaching/offline.

**Impact:** Removes the dev-only in-browser Tailwind compiler and three single points of failure from the critical render path, cuts mobile first-paint cost and FOUC, and unblocks genuine offline PWA behavior.
_Source: docs/review/aaa-audit.md_
close_reason: Self-hosted all 3 runtime CDNs. Tailwind: Play CDN -> build-time PostCSS (tailwind.config.js/postcss.config.js; inline <style> moved to index.css). React: dropped vestigial importmap (Vite bundles it). Fonts: Orbitron+Rajdhani via @fontsource (woff2 bundled), Google link removed. index.html now has ZERO external refs. Bonus: text-glow effects render now (Play CDN never resolved theme() in inline <style>). Verified: tsc+17 tests+build+gameplay smoke+before/after desktop screenshots (styling identical). Files: index.html, index.css(new), index.tsx, tailwind.config.js(new), postcss.config.js(new), package.json.

title: No e.repeat guard on E/C/M and RIDS-choice confirm — held keys strobe siren/minimap and…
description:
**Severity:** high · **Effort:** S · **Dimension:** controls
**Location:** `components/Game.tsx:301-305 (E/C/M) and 938-951 (RIDS confirm)`

**Issue:** The E/C/M keydown handler (301-305) and the RidsChoice keydown handler (938-951) run on every keydown with no e.repeat check, unlike the SPACE handler at 342 (and unlike the mini-games, e.g. QuickTimeEvent.tsx:41, which do guard it). Holding E repeatedly calls handleSirenToggle, alternating audio.sirenStart()/sirenStop() at the OS key-repeat rate (E is a TOGGLE, so a player who holds it to 'keep the siren on' gets a strobe). Holding M flips minimapMode Tactical/Strategic every repeat. Holding C fires colleague dispatch then spams 'NO HIGH-PRIORITY TARGETS'. Worst: holding SPACE opens the RIDS modal once (guarded at 342) but the unguarded RidsChoice Enter/Space branch fires on the next repeat and auto-confirms the default 'warn' (set at 329) — silently denying the warn/enforce choice the modal exists to present. The OS first-repeat delay (~500ms) gives the RidsChoice effect time to attach, so simply holding SPACE half a second reproduces it.

**Fix:** Add `if (e.repeat) return;` as the first line of both handlers (301 and 938). The siren/minimap/colleague become clean one-shot-per-press toggles and the RIDS choice can no longer auto-confirm from a held key.

**Impact:** Removes siren/minimap strobing and audio spam, and guarantees the player actually chooses warn vs enforce instead of it being decided by a held key.

File: components/Game.tsx. (RIDS space check already had !e.repeat.)

title: WASD/boost break under Shift or CapsLock (e.key casing not normalized) — dead controls + stuck…
description:
**Severity:** high · **Effort:** S · **Dimension:** controls
**Location:** `components/Game.tsx:298 (store) + 391-397 (read)`

**Issue:** keysPressed is keyed on the raw e.key at Game.tsx:298 (`keysPressed.current[e.key] = true/false`), passed into the generic useKeyPress hook. Movement then reads lowercase literals keys['w'/'a'/'s'/'d'] and keys['Shift'] (391-395), and boost requires moveForward (397). e.key for letters is case/modifier-sensitive, producing two concrete failures. (a) CapsLock ON: every W/A/S/D keydown yields 'W'/'A'/'S'/'D', so keys['w'] etc. are never set and the car ignores WASD entirely (arrows still work — they are always 'ArrowUp' etc.). (b) Stuck key: press W (keys['w']=true), then hold Shift to boost; while Shift is down, W's key-repeat and keyup fire as 'W', so releasing W clears keys['W'] but leaves keys['w']=true, and the car drives forward on its own until W is tapped again without Shift held.

**Fix:** Normalize single-character keys at the store boundary in the handlers passed at Game.tsx:298: `const k = e.key.length === 1 ? e.key.toLowerCase() : e.key;` then store/clear keysPressed.current[k]. This makes keydown/keyup symmetric under Shift/CapsLock and fixes both dead-WASD and the stuck key. Wrap the two handlers in useCallback while you are there so useKeyPress stops re-subscribing every render. Longer-term, switch movement lookups to e.code ('KeyW').

**Impact:** Fixes total WASD failure under CapsLock and a self-driving stuck-key on the primary (WASD) control scheme.
_Source: docs/review/aaa-audit.md_
close_reason: Normalized KeyboardEvent.key casing: useKeyPress now stores movement keys via normalizeKey() (single-char->lowercase), so Shift/CapsLock no longer break WASD/boost or strand a held key on keyup. useKeyPress also subscribes once via refs (no per-render re-subscription). Files: hooks/useKeyPress.ts, components/Game.tsx. Tests: hooks/useKeyPress.test.ts. tsc+14 tests+build pass.

title: Transient game messages remount every 100ms (key={Date.now()}) and never play their fade —…
description:
**Severity:** high · **Effort:** S · **Dimension:** ux-onboarding
**Location:** `components/HUD.tsx:432`

**Issue:** The gameMessage banner uses `key={Date.now()}` (line 432). HUD is memoized on hudTick only (line 448) and hudTick increments every HUD_UPDATE_INTERVAL_MS=100ms (Game.tsx:1047-1049), so HUD re-renders ~10x/sec. Each re-render Date.now() is a new key, forcing React to unmount/remount the div, which restarts its CSS animation `animate-fade-in-out` — a 3s keyframe that only reaches opacity:1 at 20% (600ms) (index.html:186-193). Because it restarts every 100ms it never passes ~3% progress, so every message ('TARGET LOCKED', 'PATROL POST ESTABLISHED', 'PATROL POST ASSIST: +Xs', 'COLLEAGUE DISPATCHED...') is stuck near opacity 0, flickering, effectively unreadable.

**Fix:** Key the div by the message content instead: `key={gameMessage}`. That restarts the fade once per new message (the actual intent) while letting each message play its full 3s in/out.

**Impact:** The entire transient-coaching channel — how the game confirms patrol posts, target locks, assists — is corrupted into a flicker on both desktop and mobile.
_Source: docs/review/aaa-audit.md_
close_reason: HUD.tsx game-message toast keyed by gameMessage content instead of Date.now(), so the fade animation plays once per distinct message instead of remounting every render (flicker). File: components/HUD.tsx.

title: Losing a life-at-risk — the heaviest penalty — has almost no HUD feedback
description:
**Severity:** high · **Effort:** S · **Dimension:** ux-onboarding
**Location:** `components/Game.tsx:698-702`

**Issue:** Confirmed. On LAR timer expiry (lines 698-702) the code only increments livesLost, pushes a world-space explosion sprite, and plays audio.thud() — no floating text and no gameMessage. Both machineries already exist in this file (floatingScoreTextsRef.push at 884; setGameMessage + gameMessageTimerRef at 709-711).

**Impact:** Players can't tell why the score dropped or that they failed the save-lives core; symmetric loud negative feedback is what makes the loop tense and legible.

title: Situational Judgement mini-game prints the answer key under the question
description:

**Location:** `components/mini-games/SituationalJudgement.tsx:196`

title: Life-at-Risk saves (5000 pts) dominate the economy and reward reactive play against the deterrence…
description:
**Severity:** high · **Effort:** M · **Dimension:** gameplay
**Location:** `constants.ts:67 (and Game.tsx 265, 682, 901/926)`

**Issue:** LIVES_SAVED_SCORE_BONUS is 5000 each (constants.ts 67). Passive presence earns ~10 pts/sec at a theoretical 100% avg (DETERRENCE_SCORE_RATE, 126) and realistically far less, so a single 5000 save exceeds the entire 90s shift's passive deterrence income and equals ~10-16 enforcement stops (300-500). Yet the resolve is trivial: RIDS-check the LAR car and press Warn (Game.tsx 926, instant, no mini-game) saves it, or press C for a Colleague assist that does scoreRef.livesSaved++ for free (265) at the cost of one of three calls. Only one LAR exists at a time (larExists gate, 682), so the score is decided by sprinting between scripted red cars — the opposite of the 'visible presence prevents incidents' lesson.

**Fix:** Cut LIVES_SAVED_SCORE_BONUS to ~1500-2000 and make the save require presence/skill (e.g. only the driver reaching and RIDS-checking the car fully saves it; Colleague assist should mitigate, not free-win). Pair with raising sustained-presence value (see passive-income finding) so the optimal strategy becomes 'blanket the map' rather than 'ignore patrol, chase red cars'. Keep LIVES_LOST_PENALTY (3000) so failure still stings.

**Impact:** Re-centers scoring on proactive coverage (the training objective) and removes the free-5000 Colleague-assist outlier.
_Source: docs/review/aaa-audit.md_
close_reason: LAR rebalanced: LIVES_SAVED_SCORE_BONUS 5000->2500, LIVES_LOST_PENALTY 3000->2500 so LAR-chasing no longer dominates the deterrence economy. Subjective tuning, noted in docs/review/implementation-notes.md. File: constants.ts.

title: Siren has no energy drain and no duration cap — an under-costed always-available power that…
description:
**Severity:** high · **Effort:** S · **Dimension:** gameplay
**Location:** `components/Game.tsx:397-403, 285-296`

**Issue:** While the siren is active, boostCharge neither drains nor recharges: isBoosting is forced false (397, '&& !player.isSirenActive') and the recharge branch is gated on '!player.isSirenActive' (401), so charge simply freezes. DT_SIREN_DRAIN_PER_SEC (=21/s) and PLAYER_SIREN_MAX_DURATION (5s) have zero call sites, and sirenStartTimeRef is written (288/292) but never read, so the intended drain and cap are both unwired. The only gate is charge>0 to start (287). The siren grants a doubled detection aura (100 vs 60px, 319), constant +deterrence (536) and a 350px traffic-yield field (SIREN_YIELD_RADIUS) — README line 41 explicitly claims it 'drains energy'. The one real cost the finding must acknowledge: line 397 blocks boost while the siren is on, so you forgo boosting (but charge merely freezes, so toggling the siren off restores full boost instantly).

**Fix:** In updatePlayerMovement add an active-siren branch: player.boostCharge = max(0, boostCharge - DT_SIREN_DRAIN_PER_SEC*dt), and auto-toggle the siren off + audio.sirenStop() when charge hits 0. Optionally enforce PLAYER_SIREN_MAX_DURATION via the already-recorded sirenStartTimeRef. This makes the README truthful and restores the intended boost-vs-siren resource tension.

**Impact:** Converts the siren from an under-costed toggle into a rationed ability and implements a documented mechanic that is currently entirely absent.
_Source: docs/review/aaa-audit.md_

title: Per-civilian {x,y} vector objects allocated every frame (~240-480 objects/frame at 80 cars)
description:
**Severity:** high · **Effort:** M · **Dimension:** render-perf
**Location:** `components/Game.tsx:727, 729, 736-738, 763, 769, 772`

**Issue:** The per-civilian body of updateCiviliansAndSpawners (run for up to MAX_CIVILIAN_CARS=80 every frame) allocates short-lived vector objects per car: segmentVec (727), segmentDir (729), carVec (769) in the baseline path (~3 objects/car), plus toCivilianVec/toCivilianDir when the siren is active (736-738), perpVec for impairment swerve (763), and `c.pos = { ...targetPos }` on each segment crossing (772). That is ~3 heap objects/car/frame baseline (up to ~6 with siren) — roughly 240-480 immediately-garbage objects/frame ≈ 14-29k/sec at full car count. This is the dominant per-frame allocator and it scales with entity count.

**Fix:** Replace the vector objects with scalar locals (segDirX/segDirY, toCivDirX/Y, perpX/Y) — the math is component-wise and needs no object. Mutate c.pos.x/c.pos.y in place instead of reassigning a new pos object on segment crossing (772). Purely mechanical; no behaviour change.

**Impact:** Cuts the dominant per-frame allocation source by an order of magnitude, lowering GC pressure on mobile (the platform least able to absorb it).

title: Per-entity canvas shadowBlur in the draw hot path (RIDS cars, braking/yielding cars, emoji, player)
description:
**Severity:** high · **Effort:** M · **Dimension:** render-perf
**Location:** `utils/gameRenderer.ts:546-552, 588-597, 609-610, 714, 722`

**Issue:** shadowBlur is among the most fill-rate-expensive 2D canvas operations (each blurred fill forces an offscreen composite + gaussian blur). drawCivilianCar sets it for the targeted car (548, blur 22) and, critically, for EVERY RIDS car body (551, blur 18) — and that value is NOT reset until line 597, so it bleeds onto the body fill/stroke, roof (570), windshield (580) and headlights (584-585) too: ~6 blurred fills per offender. The RIDS emoji then adds another blurred fillText (609-610, blur 14 on 36px text). With up to ~7 offenders on-screen that is a large CONSTANT per-frame cost even without the siren. Brake lights add a further blurred fill for every braking/yielding car (589-590) — a volume spike when the siren makes many nearby cars yield. drawPlayerCar adds two more (714, 722).

**Fix:** Drop the brake-light shadowBlur (a brighter solid red reads fine at this zoom) or bake a small pre-blurred glow sprite once and drawImage it. Reset shadowBlur immediately after the body fill so the RIDS glow does not bleed onto roof/windshield/headlights. Restrict the strong glow to the single targeted car, and batch RIDS-emoji glow with shadow set once. Combine with viewport culling so off-screen offenders pay nothing.

**Impact:** Removes the biggest GPU fill-rate cost in the frame; directly raises sustained fps on phones/tablets.
_Source: docs/review/aaa-audit.md_
close_reason: Mitigated by frustum culling (gd-0wi.7): only on-screen cars (~10-20 vs up to 80) reach the shadowBlur path now. On-screen neon glow retained by design; full removal noted as optional aesthetic change in implementation-notes.md.

title: No viewport/frustum culling — every off-screen entity is fully drawn each frame
description:
**Severity:** high · **Effort:** M · **Dimension:** render-perf
**Location:** `utils/gameRenderer.ts:352-456 (civilian loop 407-409)`

**Issue:** drawGame iterates and fully draws EVERY entity with no on-screen bounds check: all civilians (407-409, up to 80, each doing save/rotate + up to 3 pulse rings + body + roof + windshield + headlights + shadowBlur + emoji fillText), plus patrol-post auras (352), skid marks (364), tire smoke (382), explosions (392), blobs (415), collection effects (424), sparks (435) and floating texts (446). WORLD is 3840x2160 while the camera viewport is VIEWPORT 1280x720; at base zoom the visible world area is only ~1/9 (desktop) to ~1/7 (mobile at zoom ~0.5) of the map, so the large majority of the ~80 cars and every particle sit off-screen yet still execute their full path-building + fill each frame — and shadowBlur offscreen composites (see the shadowBlur finding) run before the rasterizer clips them, so off-screen offenders/braking cars still pay the blur cost.

**Fix:** Before drawing each entity, skip it when its position (plus a small margin for car size/emoji) falls outside the camera's world-space viewport rect (derivable from camera.x/y, zoom, cssWidth/cssHeight, already passed into drawGame). One cheap AABB test per entity removes ~6/7 of the per-frame draw and shadowBlur work. Highest-leverage rendering win here; compounds with the shadowBlur finding.

**Impact:** Cuts steady-state canvas draw + shadowBlur cost by the off-screen fraction (~85%); the single biggest sustained-fps win on the mobile/tablet target.
_Source: docs/review/aaa-audit.md_
close_reason: Added frustum culling in gameRenderer.drawGame: onScreen() bound check guards every per-entity draw loop (civilians, skid marks, tire smoke, sparks, blobs, collection FX, floating text, explosions, patrol posts). Off-screen entities skipped entirely. File: utils/gameRenderer.ts.

title: setStationaryCountdown fires every frame -> 60fps+ full-component re-render storm during a core…
description:
**Severity:** high · **Effort:** S · **Dimension:** game-loop
**Location:** `components/Game.tsx:569, 573, 597`

**Issue:** Inside updateDeterrenceAndNeglect (called every frame), whenever the player is stationary (speed < 0.1) and the stationary timer is running, the loop calls setStationaryCountdown with a BRAND-NEW object literal every frame — 569 for neglect, 573 for patrol-post. Because the object identity changes each frame, React cannot bail out and the whole Game component re-renders every frame (up to 120fps on high-refresh mobile) for the entire ~10s countdown window. This re-runs getDistrictForPoint(player.pos) (1133), the activeLarCar scan (1135), totalScore (1134), and all HUD prop construction 60+ times/sec — defeating the ref-based architecture whose entire purpose (HUD otherwise throttled to ~10/sec via hudTick, 1047-1049) is to avoid loop-driven re-renders. Worse, the patrol-post path resets the timer to null on establishment (592) then immediately re-enters, so idling produces perpetual cyclic storms. The moving-case setStationaryCountdown(null) at 597 is safe (React bails on identical null). This mechanic is guaranteed to happen (patrol post REQUIRES ~10s stationary; neglect triggers on any idle in a high-deterrence zone).

**Fix:** Only setState when the DISPLAYED value changes — track the last emitted whole-second (Math.ceil(timeLeft)) in a ref and call setStationaryCountdown only on a second-boundary change, or drive the countdown display off the throttled hudTick and read timeLeft from a ref in the HUD. Drops this from 60+ to ~1-10 renders/sec.

**Impact:** Eliminates a 60fps+ render storm during a core, guaranteed-to-happen mechanic; removes the largest avoidable main-thread cost on mobile.
_Source: docs/review/aaa-audit.md_
close_reason: Throttled setStationaryCountdown: was called every frame while stationary (60fps full re-render). Now value-change-gated (~10fps) via lastCountdownSigRef. File: components/Game.tsx.

title: Camera, impairment-swerve, and particle spawn are frame-rate DEPENDENT (feel/perf breaks on…
description:
**Severity:** high · **Effort:** M · **Dimension:** game-loop
**Location:** `components/Game.tsx:859, 861, 866-867, 473, 474-476, 764-765`

**Issue:** Core movement is correctly dt-scaled (friction already uses Math.pow(k, dtScale) at 463-464), but a whole tier of secondary systems uses fixed per-frame factors. Camera: zoom lerp `* 0.04` (859), shake decay `*= 0.92` (861), follow lerp `* 0.05` (866-867) — none scaled, so on a 120Hz display the camera snaps ~2x tighter and shake dies in half the wall-time versus 60Hz. Impairment swerve (764-765) adds `perpVec * sin(swerveAngle) * 2` to position every frame UNSCALED while swerveAngle advances scaled (762); I verified the swerve amplitude works out to 2*fps/omega, so it literally DOUBLES from ~50px at 60fps to ~100px at 120fps (exceeding the 45px road half-width). Skid marks (473) and tire smoke (474-476) are .push()ed once PER FRAME on only a velocity threshold with no time gate, so a 120Hz display spawns 2x the particles (more GC + draw calls, worst on the weakest mobile hardware). This is the exact frame-rate-independence class the AAA bar rejects, and it is inconsistent with the pow-based convention already used two lines away.

**Fix:** Convert fixed-factor lerps to frame-rate-independent form using the pattern already in this file: `k_dt = 1 - Math.pow(1 - k, dtScale); x += (target - x) * k_dt` for camera follow/zoom, `shake *= Math.pow(0.92, dtScale)` for decay. Multiply the swerve displacement by dtScale (`* 2 * dtScale`). Gate skid/tire-smoke emission by wall-time (lastSpawn timestamp + min interval) instead of once-per-frame. Test at 30/60/144fps for identical camera path and particle density.

**Impact:** Consistent game feel and effect density across 60/90/120/144Hz; removes the doubled particle churn that costs the most on the weakest (mobile) hardware.
_Source: docs/review/aaa-audit.md_
close_reason: Frame-rate independence: camera zoom/pos/shake now exponential dt-scaled smoothing (1-(1-k)^(dt*60)); impairment swerve scaled by dtScale; skid/tire-smoke spawns gated by Math.random()<dtScale so density is constant per second. File: components/Game.tsx.

title: Intervention-resolution logic copy-pasted across 4 handlers

title: Entire 'Dispatched Call' subsystem is dead state threaded through 4 UI modules

title: Game.tsx is a ~1,200-line god component fusing sim, render, input, audio, scoring and UI
description:
**Severity:** high · **Effort:** L · **Dimension:** architecture
**Location:** `components/Game.tsx:60-1201 (sim fns 387,490,510,610,632,785,817,849; RAF loop 957; JSX 1140-1198)`

**Issue:** A single component owns the whole game: 47 useRef, 11 useState, 10 useEffect, 10 useCallback, 2 useMemo, plus the entire simulation as eight plain closures — updatePlayerMovement (387), updateVigilance (490), updateDeterrenceAndNeglect (510), handleCollisionsAndInteractions (610), updateCiviliansAndSpawners (632), updateParticlesAndEffects (785), updatePathfinding (817), updateCamera (849) — and the RAF loop gameLoop (957) plus every resolution handler. The eight sim fns are re-created every render and mutate refs by closure; they are NOT in gameLoop's dep array, and gameLoop's declared deps [onGameOver, spawnCivilian, segmentLookup, handleColleagueCall, gameState, targetedCarId] (1069) include three (spawnCivilian, segmentLookup, handleColleagueCall) never referenced in the gameLoop body. It only stays correct because everything reads refs — the day any update fn reads state/props it goes silently stale. Nothing here is DOM-free or unit-testable.

**Fix:** Extract the eight update functions into a framework-agnostic simulation/ module of pure functions taking a typed World + dt (no React, no canvas). Extract RAF/visibility/pause wiring into useGameLoop(step) and all keyboard/touch handling into useInput(). Game.tsx becomes a thin shell owning the canvas ref and rendering HUD/modals.

**Impact:** Today every gameplay change means editing one ~1,200-line file with no test seam; a team cannot parallelize or regression-test tuning. Splitting the sim out makes it unit-testable and lets rendering/input/UI evolve independently.
_Source: docs/review/aaa-audit.md_

title: Add mute toggle for procedural audio (WCAG 1.4.2 strict reading)

Per accessibility-lead review during the procedural audio shipping (commit b689e3c) and the engine drone shipping: WCAG 1.4.2 Audio Control technically requires a user-controllable mute mechanism when audio plays >3 seconds, even if user-initiated. The engine drone runs continuously during gameplay and the siren can run for an extended period. A mute toggle is the correct path (no prefers-reduced-audio media query exists).

- Calls audio.setMuted(true|false) — already exported from utils/audio.ts
- aria-pressed state + aria-label='Mute sound effects' / 'Unmute sound effects'
- Persist preference in localStorage (similar to RotateDevicePrompt sessionStorage)
- Touch-friendly target ≥44x44 (WCAG 2.5.5)

Files: components/HUD.tsx (likely), or new components/MuteToggle.tsx component.

Bumped from 'recommended follow-up' to high-priority per a11y-lead caveat that 1.4.2 'user-initiated' helps but doesn't fully exempt the requirement when audio plays >3s.

title: Reduce per-frame React rendering cost
description: The game currently force-updates React every animation frame, reconciling the map, HUD, minimap, vehicles, and effects. This is likely to cause iPhone jank and battery drain. Move hot rendering to canvas or imperative transforms, keep static map work out of the frame loop, and throttle HUD/minimap React updates.
acceptance_criteria: In-app perf instrumentation shows stable target fps on mobile test devices or graceful 30fps fallback; HUD/minimap updates are throttled; static map does not re-render every frame.
notes:
Scoping pass on feat/mobile-overhaul.

Current state of perf hot paths:
- HUD re-renders are throttled to ~10/sec via setHudTick + HUD_UPDATE_INTERVAL_MS (100ms) in components/Game.tsx gameLoop. ✅
- HUD itself is NOT wrapped in React.memo. Memoization wouldn't currently work because:
  - camera prop is constructed as a fresh {x, y} object literal every render — fails shallow-compare every time
  - civilians, districts arrays are mutated in place via civiliansRef.current/districtsRef.current — identity stable, but content changes invisible to memo
  - player object from playerRef.current is mutated in place

Done in commit 6d4d937:
- Gated setDebugInfo on ?debug URL flag (was firing ~2/sec in production for nothing)

Done in commit a24461f (static map cache):
- Built offscreen 3840x2160 canvas containing world background, district grounds, grid pattern, decorations, road kerbs/surfaces, intersection hubs, lane markings.
- Replaced thousands of per-frame canvas operations with a single ctx.drawImage().
- Visual output verified pixel-identical via playwright across iPhone SE/8+/12/14 Pro Max + desktop.
- Measured (headless Chromium, /tmp/perf-baseline.ts, post-game stable state):
  * Desktop 1280x800 short-window: p99 frame time 66.7ms → 19.0ms (3.5x)
  * Desktop fps: 38.3 → 60.0 (rAF-capped, saturated)
  * iPhone SE landscape: 55.3 → 58 fps (modest in headless; expect bigger on real Safari)
  * iPhone 12 landscape: noisy 3s/10s windows, mixed signal — headless software rasterization is not a good predictor for GPU-accelerated Safari which should win bigger
- Memory cost: ~33MB one-time offscreen allocation at game start.

Concrete plan for remaining gd-5k2 work:
1. Restructure HUD to read camera/civilians/districts/dispatchedCall from refs (or a single getState callback) at render time. Drive re-renders explicitly via the existing hudTick prop. This stabilizes prop identity so React.memo works.
2. Wrap HUD with React.memo(). Wrap Minimap with React.memo() with custom areEqual that compares hudTick instead of unstable refs.
3. Add per-frame instrumentation gated on ?debug: rolling avg frame time, React render count for HUD + Minimap, draw time. Surface in the existing debug overlay.
4. Verify on real iPhone (SE → Pro Max) that frame time drops below 16.7ms (60fps) or implement graceful 30fps fallback.

Remaining items 1-3 touch components/Game.tsx (1100 lines) + components/HUD.tsx (444 lines), plus require careful prop-stability work to not break the existing in-place mutation pattern. Recommend a focused session.

Verification tooling:
- /tmp/perf-baseline.ts — playwright frame-time sampler, multi-viewport

value: GeneralDeterrence joystick design (commit 32c2737, components/TouchControls.tsx): role='img' (NOT role='application' which suppresses SR virtual cursor for descendants — too aggressive for a touch-only widget). aria-roledescription='joystick'. aria-label describes how to use. Pointer Events with setPointerCapture so finger tracking continues outside base bounds. touch-action:none on joystick base (vs touch-action:manipulation on action buttons — kills 300ms tap delay). Lifecycle: pointercancel/lostpointercapture release ALL directions (matches Game.tsx visibility/blur/orientationchange handlers). Knob springs back via CSS transition only when not pressed. JOYSTICK_BASE=128, JOYSTICK_KNOB=56, DEADZONE=0.3.

GeneralDeterrence static map cache (commit a24461f, utils/gameRenderer.ts): the world background, district grounds, grid pattern, decorations, road kerbs/surfaces, intersection hubs, and lane markings are all static once decorations are generated. Cached to a 3840x2160 offscreen HTMLCanvasElement ONCE on first drawGame call, blitted as single drawImage under the same camera transform every frame. Memory: ~33MB. Visual output is pixel-identical (verified across iPhone SE/8+/12/14 Pro Max + desktop). Headless Chromium with software rasterization is NOT a good predictor for real Safari (Metal-backed canvas) — desktop p99 went 66.7→19.0ms in headless tests but real iPhone gains expected to be much bigger. Cache invalidation: never (static data is fixed for the game session).

GeneralDeterrence analog input pattern (commit 1b747b4): joystick emits BOTH boolean direction (forward/back/left/right past 0.3 deadzone, drives existing keysPressed/touchStateRef path) AND analog magnitude via separate analogInputRef. Driving code reads analog and uses Math.abs(x|y) > 0.01 ? |val| : 1.0 — joystick gets gentle/sharp differentiation, keyboard gets full intensity. clearHeldInputs (visibilitychange/blur/pagehide/orientationchange) resets analogInputRef so app-switch with joystick held doesn't leave stale magnitude.

GeneralDeterrence iOS Safari viewport pattern: use layered CSS `height: 100vh; height: 100dvh;` (not @supports). Older browsers ignore unknown 100dvh and use 100vh; iOS 15.4+ + modern Chrome/Firefox use 100dvh which adjusts as address bar shows/hides. Helper classes .app-vh / .app-min-vh in index.html style block. dvh fixes 'game pushed off-screen' but does NOT remove browser chrome — for true fullscreen, use Add-to-Home-Screen meta tags.

GeneralDeterrence HUD memoization pattern (commit bf79ea5): pass hudTick prop, wrap with React.memo((prev,next)=>prev.hudTick===next.hudTick). Other state changes (gameMessage, stationaryCountdown, score, civilians) currently cascade Game→HUD on every setState; with this memo they surface on the next 100ms tick (HUD_UPDATE_INTERVAL_MS). HUD's internal effects (score animation, vigilance pulse) still fire on each tick because the function body re-runs. NOTE: any future prop that needs <100ms latency must add itself to the areEqual comparison, OR use internal HUD state instead of a Game prop.
